statement: Find the total area enclosed between the curves $y=\\sin x$ and $y=\\cos x$ for $0\\le x\\le \\tfrac{\\pi}{2}$.
solution: The curves cross at $x=\\tfrac{\\pi}{4}$. Area $=\\int_{0}^{\\pi/4}(\\cos x-\\sin x)\\,dx+\\int_{\\pi/4}^{\\pi/2}(\\sin x-\\cos x)\\,dx$. First part $= [\\sin x+\\cos x]_{0}^{\\pi/4}=(\\tfrac{\\sqrt2}{2}+\\tfrac{\\sqrt2}{2})-1=\\sqrt2-1$. Second part $= [-\\cos x-\\sin x]_{\\pi/4}^{\\pi/2}=(-1)-(-\\sqrt2)=\\sqrt2-1$. Total $=2(\\sqrt2-1)$.
hints: Find where $\\sin x=\\cos x$ in the interval.
Integrate the upper minus lower curve on each sub-interval.
